query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a modest amount of a carefully chosen alloying addition into phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys will improve both their glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the resulting amorphous state.
generation.material_initial_state: A phosphorus-containing high-entropy (or compositionally complex) alloy prepared under standard rapid-quenching conditions that exhibits marginal glass-forming ability and thermal stability.
generation.intervention: Add a low concentration (on the order of a few atomic percent) of an additional element selected for its large atomic size mismatch and strong chemical interactions with phosphorus and the other constituent elements.
generation.conditions: Under identical melt processing conditions (e.g., rapid quenching) and within the compositional regime where the base alloy forms a glass, the intervention should improve both the maximum casting thickness (a proxy for glass-forming ability) and the onset temperature of crystallization (a proxy for thermal stability). This effect is expected as long as the additive level is low enough to avoid secondary phase formation.
generation.structural_mediator: An increased atomic packing disorder and disruption of medium-range ordering that normally facilitates crystallization.
generation.mechanism: The additive is hypothesized to act by increasing the kinetic barrier for crystallization via enhanced local structural disorder. This disruption in the arrangement of atoms suppresses nucleation events during cooling and retards devitrification upon heating.
generation.predicted_outcome: An alloy with the additive will display a higher critical casting thickness and an increased crystallization onset temperature (Tx) compared to the baseline phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy without the additive.
generation.baseline: Phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy of similar composition prepared under the same processing conditions without the additional minor alloying element.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is anticipated only within a narrow concentration range of the additive and under rapid-quenching conditions; concentrations that are too high or alternative processing methods (e.g., very slow cooling) may not yield the improvement or might even induce crystallinity.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of the improvement and the optimal concentration range of the additive remain uncertain and may depend on the specific choice of element. There is also uncertainty as to whether the hypothesized disruption of medium-range order is the dominant mechanism in this system.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples using identical rapid-quenching protocols: one set using the baseline phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy and a second set with an additional low concentration (e.g., 2–5 at%) of the chosen alloying element. Characterize both sample sets for critical casting thickness and crystallization onset temperature using standardized techniques.
measurements: Critical casting thickness (e.g., via casting trials or imaging of sample cross-sections)
Crystallization onset temperature (Tx) measured by differential scanning calorimetry (DSC)
X-ray diffraction (XRD) to confirm amorphous structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples with the minor alloying addition do not show a statistically significant increase in both the critical casting thickness and the crystallization onset temperature relative to the baseline, the hypothesis that the additive improves glass-forming ability and thermal stability is falsified.
